title: Format Order Summary
prompt: A C# ASP.NET order API needs a compact summary for orders. Write a function that returns the number followed by the id in square brackets, like "Alpha [1]".

explanation.beginner:
Example: formatOrderSummary({"id":"1","number":"Alpha"}) produces "Alpha [1]". Choose the numeric contribution of each record, then combine those contributions using the contract’s initial value.

Compare “uses the provided id”: input [{"id":"42","number":"Beta"}] produces "Beta [42]". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Choose the numeric contribution of each record, then combine those contributions using the contract’s initial value.

Tempting mistake: A count of records is not a sum of their values. Test empty input and a zero-valued record separately.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “uses the provided id”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
